feed.title: VERAQIS Research
feed.subtitle: Measurements of what is and is not recoverable from damaged files, including the negative results.

entry.title: A deleted row's identity, from b-tree shape alone
entry.summary: On a fixture where the key is never derivable from the content, 100 of 100 deleted rowids were reconstructed exactly — using only cell ordering and separator keys.

entry.title: An end record that belongs to a different archive
entry.summary: A ZIP inside a ZIP carries its own end record. Destroy the outer one and a reader can anchor on the inner archive, then list two files from the wrong container.

entry.title: The database that cannot prove it is current
entry.summary: Copy a SQLite file without its -wal and the rows still read perfectly — they are just not necessarily the latest. When currency is provable, and when it is not.

entry.title: The table a recovery tool looks straight past
entry.summary: A WITHOUT ROWID table is stored as an index b-tree. Our own recovery returned 0 of its 4 rows and reported no error. What that costs, and how it was found.

entry.title: We ran the federal SQLite forensics spec on ourselves
entry.summary: Six fixtures, 13 core assertions, 126 results — including the two we fail and the 23 we do not answer. What the specification measures, and what it cannot ask.

entry.title: What an index proves when the table is gone
entry.summary: An index is a second copy of part of your data. It can prove a row existed and what its key was — and it must never be allowed to supply the rest of the row.

entry.title: When "provable" does not mean "current"
entry.summary: A hot rollback journal makes the committed state provable — and the rows sitting in the database file are the uncommitted ones. Why the obvious rule is wrong.

entry.title: Why we refuse to follow a chain we can see
entry.summary: A disconnected page points at the rest of its record. Following that pointer needs a second, independent witness — and without one the engine abstains.

entry.title: Bit flip in a solid 7z archive: what survives
entry.summary: We flipped one bit at six depths in a real 541-file solid 7z archive and counted what still decodes byte-exact: 87 to 501 files recovered, zero false files.

entry.title: The joint-verifier surface is empty — 12 formats
entry.summary: Can independent checksums be combined to solve for lost bytes? We measured 12 file formats: the joint-sufficient share is 0.00 in every one, so the solver was cancelled.

entry.title: Recovering past corruption in xz and bzip2
entry.summary: Stock xz -d abandons a whole stream on one bad block. We measured block-independent salvage: 9 of 10 blocks recovered, each CRC-verified, zero false bytes.

entry.title: CRC-32 collisions that pass gzip -t and unzip -t
entry.summary: We built files with different contents and identical CRC-32 that pass gzip -t and unzip -t. What a passing checksum proves, what it cannot, and what closes the gap.
